source_evidence: Another type of retirement saving account is one that you set up yourself, known as an Individual Retirement Account or IRA. You can invest in your own tax-advantaged investment account to provide financial security when you retire. IRA contributions can also reduce the amount you pay in taxes.
answer: An Individual Retirement Account (IRA) is a retirement savings account you set up yourself. It is tax-advantaged, and contributions may reduce the amount of taxes you pay. After contributing, you choose how to invest the money in the account. You can have both an IRA and an employer-provided retirement plan, though annual contribution limits apply.
